metadata.title: One Word That Oversold My Paper
metadata.audience: Students and practitioners learning to use and report on AI systems
metadata.fellow: Janvi Chitroda, AI Data Engineer volunteer, Medhavy project, Humanitarians AI
metadata.source: inbox/term2-week01/term2-week1-video-content.md (primary, sha256 15a84b4b…); SOURCE-LOCKED-FACTS.md (Janvi's locked facts, 2026-10-27); supporting: inbox/week-01/RESULTS.md, DESIGN.md, AGREEMENT_METRICS.md
metadata.note: Project update. Thesis: writing about your own system forces you to say what it actually measures; the first draft claimed more than the system can prove. WORDING LAW: the definitions are never called verified/correct/accurate/reliable; those words appear only inside the verbatim BEFORE sentence, as the words to audit, or explicitly negated (ASSUMPTIONS.md A6). Nothing after Week 1 is mentioned.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude composer, ask lands answered. Required fellow intro line + AI-narration disclosure + teammate credit.
beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Janvi and this video is about one word that oversold my technical paper. This narration is an AI-generated voice; the work is mine. My teammate Thejus built the definition-generation pipeline, and I built the QA pipeline. This week I spent 22 hours writing it up in about 4,500 words.

beats.narration_text: Writing my paper made me say what my system actually measures: three AI judges reached consensus on 8,053 keywords. My first draft claimed more than that, and it started with one word.

beats.role_note: What the system does, in one beat: the textbook popups, three judges (logos), five tags, 2-of-3 majority, all-differ flagged for human review, 94.2% of 10,049 rows resolved by majority.
beats.narration_text: The pipeline sorts keyword popup definitions for the Medhavy cancer biology textbook. Three judges from three providers, Mistral Small, G P T four o mini and Claude three point five Sonnet, each pick one of five tags. If two agree, that tag wins. If all three differ, it is flagged for human review. Across 10,049 rows, 94.2 percent resolved by majority.
beats.visual_intent: Top: one keyword-popup definition card (Medhavy cancer biology textbook). Middle: three judge columns with Mistral / OpenAI / Claude logos and model names. Bottom: the five tag chips. Case 1: approved / approved / supplementary, the two matches link, 'approved' wins. Case 2: three different tags, 'all 3 differ → flagged for human REVIEW'. Then the count: 10,049 rows, 94.2% resolved by majority, 5.8% flagged.

beats.role_note: BEFORE and AFTER verbatim; the overselling words struck, the replacement words highlighted; both held side by side.
beats.narration_text: Here is the sentence from my first draft. 'Verified' implies the definitions were confirmed against the truth. 'Demonstrating high reliability' implies the system measures whether they are right. Neither is true. It shows that three models agreed with each other. So the rewrite says exactly that: 94.2 percent inter-model agreement, with 8,053 keywords reaching consensus for inclusion.

beats.role_note: The three limitations the overselling sentence was hiding.
beats.narration_text: That old sentence also skipped past what my Limitations section says. There is no gold standard, so I measured agreement, not expert-checked accuracy. If all three judges share a blind spot, the vote cannot see it. And G P T four o mini helped generate some definitions and also judged them, which risks self-preference.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed, read aloud verbatim, then discussed.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here is my results section. Find every verified, accurate or reliable. For each one, tell me what my metric actually measures, and rewrite the sentence to claim only that. Watch for agreement or coverage described as proof the output is right. Run it on your own results.
